perplexity.description:
EP Two is a four-track extended play by Paul Draper, released in November 2016 on Kscope. The EP marked the second installment in a pair of releases that preceded his debut solo album, following EP One earlier that year after a twelve-year absence from recording. Recorded and produced by Draper at his studio The Kitchen, the project showcases a return to the melodic sensibilities that defined his work with Mansun while exploring new sonic territory.

The EP's musical palette spans multiple approaches to rock composition. "Friends Make The Worst Enemies," co-written with Catherine AD of The Anchoress, delivers what was described as a "knock-out punch" of "relentless chasmic melody and autobiographical melancholy." "Some Things Are Better Left Unsaid" operates as a spacious ballad that transitions from delicate acoustic arrangements to bass-driven, echo-chamber noise, while "Don't You Wait It Might Never Come" presents a surging rock and roll number. The EP also includes an acoustic rendition of "Friends Make The Worst Enemies," providing an alternative interpretation of the lead track.

EP Two functioned as a strategic preview of Draper's full-length debut, Spooky Action, which arrived in spring 2017. The two EPs together established the sonic direction and thematic concerns that would define his solo work, bridging his celebrated Mansun era with a new chapter in his career.
